title: Filter Open Ports with Lambda
description: Use lambda and filter() to extract only open ports from a list of scan results.
problemStatement:
Assume a list of tuples `scan_results = [("192.168.1.1", 22, True), ("192.168.1.1", 23, False), ("192.168.1.2", 80, True), ("192.168.1.2", 443, False)]` where each tuple is (host, port, is_open). Use `filter()` with a lambda to create a new list containing only the entries where `is_open` is True. Print the filtered list.

Then, using `map()` and a lambda, transform the filtered list into a list of strings formatted like "host:port (open)". Print that list.
hints: filter: `lambda entry: entry[2]` (since entry[2] is the boolean).
Wrap filter/map with list() to see results.
solutionCode:
scan_results = [("192.168.1.1", 22, True), ("192.168.1.1", 23, False), ("192.168.1.2", 80, True), ("192.168.1.2", 443, False)]

open_entries = list(filter(lambda e: e[2], scan_results))
print(open_entries)

formatted = list(map(lambda e: f"{e[0]}:{e[1]} (open)", open_entries))
print(formatted)
